newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela president to mull tanker detentions - P&I.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela president to mull tanker detentions - P&I.

text.p: International concerns over the detention of two oil tankers by Venezuela will be addressed by the country's president, protection and indemnity (P&I) insurers said Monday.

The International Group of P&I Clubs, which represents shipping cargo insurers, said a delegation to Caracas had received assurances from Venezuela's foreign minister that the issue will be put before the president.
"Foreign Minister Dr Miguel Angel Burelli-Rivas undertook to discuss immediately the problem with the President of Venezuela," the International Group said.

The Greek-owned tanker Nissos Amorgos and its captain, Konstantino Spiropoulos, have been detained in Venezuela for five months since the ship spilled around 25,000 barrels of oil after grounding in the Maracaibo Channel. Another tanker, the Plate Princess, which spilled 20 barrels of oil in late May, is also being held.

P&I Clubs representing the ships' owners have posted guarantees in the Venezuelan courts up to the full limits of the owners' liability under the international convention to which Venezuela is a signatory, the insurers said.
Director of Norway's Gard P&I Club Sara Burgess said the insurers were pleased at the response by the Foreign Ministry in setting up meetings.
"We hope these discussions will result in a speedy resolution of the current problems," she said.

"We need to discuss with the Venezuelan authorities how the legal procedures for dealing with claims relating to oil spills should be dealt with, both now and in the future, to ensure there is no repetition of the long delays experienced by the Nissos Amorgos and Plate Princess," she added.
The delegation from Gard and the Standard Club of the UK also met representatives of other ministries and the country's oil industry.
Tanker owners have expressed concern at the poor state of the dredging of the Maracaibo Channel, through which about 70 percent of Venezuela's oil exports flow.
Venezuelan authorities have recently increased the allowed navigable depths for tankers in the channel to 37.3 feet, from a restricted depth of 36 feet imposed after groundings in February and March.

The depth increase is aimed at allowing larger tankers to transit waterway and help the flow of oil exports but a recent Venezuelan Navy report, which Reuters has seen, suggests the channel's banks are more compact than they should be and there are large metallic objects in the area where the groundings occurred.
